text: why is it so hard to read the Bible with fresh eyes hey everybody I'm Dan mclen I'm a scholar of the Bible and religion and in a recent video I pointed out that
the narrative in Genesis 4 makes pretty clear that Cain's wife was not another
child of Adam and Eve and someone posted this insightful comment on that video hey Dan mclen I was wondering if you
could address why is it that when we read the Bible none of this Dawns on us we just read it and it makes perfect sense to us and it isn't until someone
else points it out that the light bulb finally goes off and this is a wonderful question because this is the beginning
of the realization that reading a text and particularly texts like the Bible is not a process of just extracting meaning
from a text that contains meaning because texts do not have any inherent meaning reading a text is a process of
creating meaning with the text because the texts are just collections of squiggles or bumps on a page or sound
waves or light bouncing off of hand signals and our job as the reader is to
convert those squiggles those bumps those sound waves those light waves into semantic content which means we must
appeal to our knowledge of and experience with agreements that have been arrived at by different groups of people regarding what kind of semantic
or conceptual content is going to be associated with what squiggle on a page bumps on a page sound waves or light
waves and those can differ from group to group from time to time even for the same squiggles or the same bumps or the
same sound waves or the same light waves and this is why people will sometimes read a text and say I just noticed this and I never noticed it before because
each time we approach the text we are constructing the meaning all over again now what governs the construction of
that meaning is the interpretive lenses that we bring to a text and the more experience with and expectations
regarding a text that we bring the more interpretive lenses we bring and so if we have rules about what a text is
allowed to say and not allowed to say or enough experience with the text to feel like we already understand the narrative then we're going to bring a whole load
of interpretive lenses that are going to mute anything that complicates those expectations and those experiences that
we bring to a text and this is why some of the best prepared people to help us understand texts a new are people who do
not have those experiences are not aware of the rules regarding what a text is and is not allowed to say which is why
children frequently ask questions that then get conditioned out of them by adults who say no no no you just don't
understand it doesn't mean that don't read it that way you're supposed to understand it this way way this is what the text is allowed to say so with texts
like the Bible most of the time we're not following the text where it is going we're grabbing the text by the hand and
we're showing it where it's going to go and this is why it is so hard to try to remove our biases and to try to read the
text with fresh eyes because we can't just tell those lenses to go away it doesn't work like that what we have to
do is learn to understand what lenses are there and then learn to correct for those lenses and that is a very
difficult thing that requires an awful lot of training an awful lot of discipline and this is also why you can't really prove anything about
interpretation the best you can do is weigh probabilities and then make a case for why the particular reading for which
you're advocating is more likely than another reading and this again makes things like biblical scholarship
incredibly complex incredibly nuanced incredibly difficult but if you're not even aware that that going on then you're not going to take that seriously
you're just going to think that your intuitions about the text which come from all of those interpretive lenses is
just the obvious answer and that's why there are so many folks who so dogmatically oppose an academic approach
to the Bible it's because it conflicts with those interpretive lenses and they have not yet learned to think critically about them I hope that's a satisfactory
answer to your wonderful question thank you so much much for posting that and the fit for this video has been The Death of Superman
